_comment: Roster for /vr-youtubers. Every subscriber count, video count, and lastUpload here was read directly from the channel's own YouTube page and RSS feed on the lastVerified date. No figure is taken from another list. Re-verify on the 90-day cadence registered in page-maintenance.json and move anyone who has gone quiet into the 'dormant' group rather than deleting them.

creators.name: Nathie
creators.note: The biggest generalist in VR video, and the one most likely to decide which story the rest of the audience hears about. On August 13 he put the WinlatorXR Half-Life 2 result in front of a mass audience, over footage he credited to Hostile VR rather than passing off as his own. We know the timeline on that one because we were reporting it the same week.

creators.name: Naysy
creators.note: The second largest active English VR channel, and the one that keeps testing the question everyone actually has rather than the one that makes a better thumbnail. Ran "Can The Steam Machine Run VR Games?" on August 2 and followed it with "Does VR work on Steam Machine?" on August 10, which is two passes at a hardware question most coverage answered once and moved on from.

creators.name: ThisKory
creators.note: The smallest English channel here and one of the most useful. Weekly VR News goes out every week whether or not the week deserved it, and the August 5 edition led with Half-Life 2 VR running standalone on Steam Frame. He also writes actual setup guides, like the UEVR walkthrough for Halo: Campaign Evolved on July 25.

creators.name: Beardo Benjo
creators.note: Owns the modding beat by simply being there constantly. Four videos in four days in mid August: Cyberpunk 2077 VR twice, then Mirror's Edge VR, then BioShock Infinite VR. If a flat game gets a VR layer, this is usually where it surfaces first.

creators.name: Gamertag VR
creators.note: 2,500 videos, the highest count on this page. Reviews land in a blunt buy, wait for a sale, or ignore format, which is more useful than a score. The Bootstrap Island review on PSVR2 ran August 13, the same day he covered the VR Games Showcase.

creators.name: Without Parole
creators.note: 3,500 videos, almost all of it PlayStation VR2. Nobody else on this page owns that platform, and PSVR2 owners are the audience most often left out of general VR coverage. Predicted the VR Games Showcase on a podcast, then hosted a live watch-along of it on August 13.

creators.name: Cas and Chary XR
creators.note: Renamed the channel from Cas and Chary VR to Cas and Chary XR, which is the whole industry shift compressed into one letter. The August 9 video is titled "Maybe We've Been Building Headsets Wrong," and that willingness to question the category rather than just rate the products is why they are here.

creators.name: MRTV
creators.note: The longest-running headset reviewer still working, and the one most willing to say a small headset beats an expensive one. Posted "We Are Not Just Reviewing VR Anymore" on July 26, then backed the point up with a review arguing the $799 URXR One matters more than Vision Pro.

creators.name: Tyriel Wood
creators.note: Has led with smart glasses for weeks straight: VITURE Pro 2, XREAL DNA, and a 30 day test of camera-free glasses comparing Memomind One against Even G2. That last one overlaps directly with our own Memomind One reporting, and he wore the things for a month before saying anything.

creators.name: BMFVR
creators.note: Slower cadence than the rest of the hardware group, roughly a video a week, and the tradeoff shows in how carefully the mixed reality pieces are put together. "This is what mixed reality on Quest 3 was ACTUALLY meant to be" ran July 5, followed by a smart glasses test on July 16.

creators.name: Fix My Oculus
creators.note: The practical channel, and the closest match on this page to the standard we hold ourselves to: tell people how to actually run the thing. "I Made My Quest 3 Run Steam Games Without a PC" went up August 2, alongside a steady run of hardware fixes and PCVR streaming comparisons.

creators.name: OtterWorldly
creators.note: VR fitness is a real use case that most coverage treats as a novelty, and this is the channel treating it as a routine. Turned a rowing machine into a game controller on August 10 and posts Beat Saber runs in mixed reality often enough to show what sustained play actually looks like.

creators.name: Valem Tutorials
creators.note: The Unity VR tutorial channel, currently four parts into a weekly series on building a VR multiplayer game, from network setup through distributed authority and ownership. Note that this is the tutorials channel; the main @ValemVR handle has been quiet since June and is all short-form now.

creators.name: Dilmer Valecillos
creators.note: XR development with the AI tooling angle taken seriously rather than as a gimmick. Built and shipped a VR/MR game with AI assistance in 30 days and published the result in July, then tested Unity's new CLI against Codex on August 6.

creators.name: Virtumaniacos
creators.note: The largest VR-focused channel we found anywhere in this pass, by a factor of more than four over the biggest English one, and effectively invisible in English-language VR coverage. Posted three times on August 14 alone. If you think of VR video as an English-speaking scene, this is the entry that should change your mind.

creators.name: VoodooDE VR (English)
creators.note: 2,800 videos from a German creator who owns close to every headset that has shipped and runs a separate English channel for the rest of us. Covered the Steam Machine plus Quest 3 as a Steam Frame alternative on August 12, which is the practical version of a question a lot of people are quietly asking.

creators.name: Okurasu VR
creators.note: A second-cohort Meta Quest ambassador and the first DPVR ambassador, covering the Japanese Quest scene. The August 7 video is about HeyVR.io, free WebXR games that run with no install at all, which is a corner of VR that barely registers in English coverage.

creators.name: SideBook VR
creators.note: 568 subscribers and 610 videos, which tells you everything about why this list is not ordered by size. Ran the Half-Life 2 Quest 3 standalone test on August 10, three days before that story reached a large audience, then posted an updated run and a Portal 1 test. The best argument on this page that audience and contribution are different things.

creators.name: Virtual Reality Oasis
creators.note: Nine months without an upload, and the last three are all about the Ready Or Not VR mod he built himself. One of the two or three biggest VR channels ever made stopped covering VR and started making it instead. The back catalogue of headset reviews is still worth reading.

creators.name: Syrmor
creators.note: A million subscribers across 139 videos total, which is a ratio nobody else here comes close to. The VRChat interview work is the best documentary record of what people actually do to each other inside social VR. Posts a few times a year at most, and the March 2026 upload was a full documentary.

creators.name: ThrillSeeker
creators.note: The most quotable essayist VR video has produced, and dark since March. His final upload is titled "The VR Industry's Great Reset." We are not going to pretend that is a coincidence.

creators.name: SadlyItsBradley
creators.note: One of the central figures in XR hardware leaks, and his YouTube has been quiet since January. The reporting did not stop, it moved to X, where it now happens in threads rather than uploads. Judging him by his upload schedule would tell you almost nothing about how much he still breaks.
